name: Su Tingbao
current_role: Chairman, Rongda Mining (Xinbaerhu Youqi, Hulunbuir); largest individual shareholder of Yunnan Chihong Zinc & Germanium (600497.SH)
profile: Born 1954, Inner Mongolia-based mining entrepreneur. Founded Rongda Mining in Dec 2001 (lead-zinc/non-ferrous exploration, mining and processing); in 2014 Chihong Zinc & Germanium bought his remaining 49% of Rongda for shares and cash, making him Chihong's largest individual shareholder. Has since gradually sold down part of that stake.
interesting_fact: The 2014 deal folded his privately built Rongda Mining into Chihong, one of the world's leading germanium producers, turning a private miner's stake into ~250m listed shares.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from university he worked as a fuel attendant at the Gaoqiao petrol station in Huludao, Liaoning, then in the Gaoqiao development zone's general office, before going into mining in the late 1990s.
notes: Very low-profile; Chinese-language sources only. Chihong is state-controlled (Chinalco/Yunnan Metallurgical), so its IR desk is not his office. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Deepak Babani
current_role: Managing Director, Satguru Holdings Ltd (Dubai real-estate developer); former Executive Vice Chairman/CEO, Eros Group (Dubai)
profile: Dubai-based Indian executive who spent ~43 years at Eros Group, the UAE electronics/consumer-tech distributor and retailer (a major Samsung distributor), rising to CEO and Executive Vice Chairman. Left at end-2021 and now develops residential property in Dubai via Satguru Holdings, starting with a G+14 tower in Al Furjan.
interesting_fact: He says he is not actually a shareholder of Eros despite the common assumption; he built the business as its long-time executive, including a Huawei partnership creating the 'IdeaHub' B2B device destination.
deep_cut_fact: He landed in the UAE in April 1978 aged 27, got his first job (assistant manager at Jumbo Electronics) via a walk-in interview at a starting salary of Dh2,000/month; his favourite book is 'Buffett: The Making of an American Capitalist'.
notes: Listing says 'Eros / Media & Entertainment' (Hurun India 2015), which could be confused with Eros International (Lulla family, films). This Deepak Babani is Eros Group Dubai (electronics); he has publicly said he is not an Eros shareholder, so the wealth attribution is uncertain. Featured in Entrepreneur ME 'The 100 NRIs 2026'.

name: Jonathan Hiscock
current_role: Founder, GSA Capital Partners LLP (London quant hedge fund)
profile: British quant hedge fund manager (b. 1974), Oxford maths graduate. Ran Deutsche Bank's Global Statistical Arbitrage prop-trading team, then spun it out in 2005 as GSA Capital with ~$500m and 15 colleagues. GSA now runs systematic strategies across all asset classes with a team of ~150 and repeated EuroHedge awards; Sunday Times put his wealth at £350m (2019).
interesting_fact: GSA's name literally comes from 'Global Statistical Arbitrage', the Deutsche Bank desk he ran; the Independent said he modelled the firm on idiosyncratic tech outfits like Google rather than traditional finance houses.
deep_cut_fact: When he spun GSA out of Deutsche Bank in Jan 2005, it launched with two funds and ~$500m under management; in 2021 the firm deliberately returned investor capital in its scalable 'alt beta' strategies to refocus on its core.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Pitch via GSA press enquiries; quant/compute angle (systematic trading infrastructure) could fit a data-center theme.

name: Dai Wei
current_role: Founder, ofo (defunct Beijing dockless bike-sharing company); since COVID has run small US ventures (Seattle power-bank rental; About Time Coffee, New York)
profile: Peking University graduate who co-founded ofo in 2014 with fellow PKU cycling-club members; it pioneered dockless smartphone bike-sharing, raised money from Didi, Xiaomi, Alibaba and DST and became a $1bn+ unicorn by 2017 before collapsing in 2018-19. He has since split time between China and the US, launching a power-bank rental startup in Seattle and the About Time Coffee chain in New York.
interesting_fact: The name 'ofo' was chosen because the word visually resembles a cyclist riding a bicycle; ofo grew from 2,000 bikes on the PKU campus in 2015 to a global unicorn in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: He spent a year as a volunteer teacher in Qinghai Province during his postgraduate studies; the 'ofo' name was reportedly born on 15 Feb 2014 while he was still teaching there. He met co-founders through a PKU Cycling Association outdoor trip.
notes: Sensitive history: ofo's collapse left large unrefunded user deposits and he was placed on China's debtor ('laolai') list; avoid in outreach. No published personal contact; US coffee venture largely wound down per 2023 reports. Was a WEF Young Global Leader-type profile; best route likely via mutual tech/VC contacts.

name: He Yan
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Chengdu GoldTel (Guoteng) Electronics Group and, since Jan 2025, actual controller of Chengdu Zhenxin Technology (300101.SZ, BeiDou satellite-navigation chips)
profile: Chengdu-born (1961) computer engineer turned entrepreneur. Founded Chengdu Guoteng (GoldTel) Communications in 1995 and in 2003 Guoteng Microelectronics, forerunner of Zhenxin Technology, often called China's 'first BeiDou navigation stock'. After years of legal disputes over the parent group, courts confirmed her control and she was reinstated as Zhenxin's actual controller in Jan 2025.
interesting_fact: Her group built an early Chinese satellite-navigation chip business (BeiDou), with GoldTel spanning communications, power, tax/finance equipment, satellite comms and IC design.
deep_cut_fact: She studied computer science at Nanjing Institute of Technology (now Southeast University), started her career in 1983 at Dongfang Electric, and is an adjunct professor at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC).
notes: Highly sensitive: arrested in 2013-14 in connection with the Li Chuncheng corruption case and served prison time; long control fight with Zhenxin management continues. Not a recommended podcast target; no published contact found.

name: Darshankumar N Patel
current_role: Founder & Chairman/MD, Vini Cosmetics (Fogg, Moov, Krack, Dermicool, Ossum), Mumbai
profile: Gujarat-born FMCG entrepreneur (known as Darshan Patel). Worked from the mid-1980s in the family business Paras Pharmaceuticals (Moov, Krack, D'Cold), sold his stake to Actis in 2006, then founded Vini Cosmetics in 2010 and launched Fogg deodorant in 2011, which became India's market leader. KKR bought a significant stake in Vini in 2021; ex-PepsiCo executive Vishal Kaul became CEO in 2022 while Patel remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Fogg disrupted India's deodorant market by being 'no gas' (more sprays per can) rather than selling seduction like Axe; its 'Fogg chal raha hai' ad line became a national catchphrase. Vini later bought back Moov, Krack and Dermicool brands.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Paras in 2006 he spent a couple of years on his 300-acre fruit orchard farm before a friend's phone call pushed him to start again; the idea for Krack came from noticing women with cracked heels at Mumbai's Churchgate station. He personally negotiates Vini's TV media deals.
notes: EY Entrepreneur of the Year India 2020 (consumer products). Low social-media presence; route via Vini Cosmetics corporate communications / KKR portfolio. No published press email found on brand sites.

name: Yang Zewen
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Nanfang Ventilator / Nanfeng Co. (300004.SZ), Foshan; family sold down below 5% in Dec 2022
profile: Nanhai (Foshan) native who in 1988, aged 42, founded a school-run factory making building fans that became Nanfang Ventilator, a leading maker of ventilation systems for metros and nuclear power plants. The Yang family took full ownership by 2005 and listed it among the first 28 ChiNext stocks in 2009 (code 300004). In Dec 2022 he and son Yang Zijiang sold 32m shares, exiting as 5%+ holders.
interesting_fact: Nanfang Ventilator was ticker 300004, one of the inaugural batch of companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in Oct 2009; its pivot to subway and nuclear-plant ventilation came in 1998 at the urging of his then 27-year-old son, a Xi'an Jiaotong nuclear graduate.
deep_cut_fact: At IPO time he drew a chairman's salary of just RMB 150,000 a year, and the family had lent the company RMB 18.58m that was converted into equity in 2005; he let his sons front the 2009 IPO roadshow while he stayed out of view.
notes: Born c.1946; alive as of the Dec 2022 share-transfer filing (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202212211581267520_1.pdf). Very private family that rarely gives interviews; company now under new control (Li Jie), so its IR is not his channel.

name: Yair Nechmad
current_role: Co-Founder, CEO and Chairman, Nayax Ltd. (Nasdaq/TASE: NYAX), Herzliya, Israel
profile: Israeli payments entrepreneur. A former Coca-Cola Israel marketing manager and head of Eden Springs (Mey Eden), he co-founded Nayax in 2005 with his brother Amir and David Ben Avi to let vending machines accept cards. Nayax listed in Tel Aviv in 2021 and on Nasdaq in 2022 and is now a global unattended-retail payments and loyalty platform (Q3 2026 revenue $128m, +23%).
interesting_fact: The founders financed their stakes with personal loans, which he calls 'very risky things on a personal level'; most of his NIS 51m from the 2021 TASE IPO went to paying them off.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1990s he was Coca-Cola Israel's marketing manager during Pepsi's entry into the Israeli market; Nayax began after a chance meeting with Ben Avi, who had rented office space in a building owned by Yair's brother Amir, and whose earlier attempt at text-message vending payments had failed.

public_contacts.value: Scott Gamm, Strategy Voice Associates - Scott@strategyvoiceassociates.com

notes: Historically interview-shy (Calcalist once noted he had never given an interview) but now appears on podcasts and in Globes. Best route: Nayax PR agency (Strategy Voice Associates) or IR (Chief Strategy Officer Aaron Greenberg).

name: Wang Zengchao
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, Chongqing Shunbo Aluminum Alloy (002996.SZ)
profile: Born 1969, Zhejiang-origin entrepreneur with 30+ years in scrap-metal recycling and secondary aluminium. Founded Shunbo in Chongqing in 2003; it listed in Shenzhen in Aug 2020 and is one of China's leading recycled-aluminium alloy producers. He co-runs it with Wang Zhenjian (chairman), both holding ~140m shares each.
interesting_fact: Shunbo was the first listed company from Chongqing's Hechuan district and the city's 56th listed firm; its business is turning scrap aluminium into alloy ingots, a low-carbon alternative to primary aluminium.
deep_cut_fact: His career began at the Xilu metal-fittings factory in Yongkang, Zhejiang; even after founding Shunbo in 2003 he worked in its purchasing department (2005-07) before becoming executive director and later chairman/GM.
notes: Facts from exchange-disclosed management bios (Eastmoney F10). Recycled aluminium/energy-intensity angle fits an energy podcast. Has been gradually selling shares (2025).

name: Tong Yihong
current_role: Director and major shareholder, Beijing Toyou Feiji Technology (同有科技, 300302.SZ); GM of Beijing Insage (英思杰) Technology
profile: Born 1964, senior engineer with a master's degree. A long-time major shareholder and director of Toyou Feiji, which grew out of Beijing Institute of Technology and calls itself China's first and only listed pure-play enterprise storage vendor (flash, domestic 'self-controllable' storage). He has run Beijing Insage Technology since 2001 and has been trimming his Toyou stake (2026).
interesting_fact: Toyou has focused on data storage for 30+ years, serving 50,000+ customers in government, finance, energy and research; it pivoted toward flash and domestically controlled storage chips/components.
deep_cut_fact: He serves as president of the Guizhou Enterprise Chamber of Commerce in Beijing, alongside his directorships at Toyou, Beijing Shengshi Quanjing and Beijing Tongxiang Anyu.
notes: Storage/data-center relevance is strong. Chairman/founder is Zhou Zexiang; Tong is the No.2 holder. IR email is the company securities office, not his personal channel.
